title: Completed local charts of an fs log regular scheme
statement: Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $\bar x$ be a geometric point over $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with residue field $k$ and characteristic monoid $P=\overline M_{\bar x}$. Choose a sharp chart $a:P\to A$ identifying $P$ with this characteristic [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart]. After replacing this sharp chart if necessary by another chart $P\to M|_{W'}$ on an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $W'$ of $\bar x$, again inducing the chosen identification of $P$ with $\overline M_{\bar x}$, there exist an integer $n\geq0$ and an isomorphism of complete local rings, compatible with $a(q)\mapsto z^q$, of the following form. If $A$ contains a field (equal characteristic) it is $\widehat A\cong B_k(P,n)$. If $A$ contains no field, then $k$ has prime characteristic $p$ (this is the mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ case) and it is $\widehat A\cong B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$, where $C$ is a Cohen ring with residue field $k$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. Here $\widehat A$ is the maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $B_L(P,n)$ denotes the completion of the monoid polynomial ring $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, with $\mathfrak m_k=0$ and $\mathfrak m_C=pC$. The monoid ring is the ring of finite sums $c z^q$ with $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. The case $P=\{0\}$ and $n=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, citing Kato (1994), Theorem 3.2 (WANTED locally). The isomorphisms respect the chart monomials; these are statements about completed strict local rings, not ordinary smooth chart maps.

proof.text: Let $a:P\to A$ be the sharp chart of [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart], defined on an affine locally Noetherian pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar x$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods] and inducing the chosen identification $P\cong\overline M_{\bar x}$; that lemma also gives that $P$ is finitely generated, integral, saturated and sharp. We take $W'=W$ and keep this chart: the replacement allowed in the statement is not needed. By the definition of a chart [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $M_{\bar x}=P\oplus_{a^{-1}(A^\times)}A^\times$, and since $P\to\overline M_{\bar x}$ is bijective and $P$ is sharp, $a(q)$ is a nonunit exactly when $q\neq0$; hence the ideal $I$ generated by the images of the nonunits of $M_{\bar x}$ is $I=(a(q):q\neq0)A$, generated by the images of finitely many generators of $P$. Log regularity at $\bar x$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] says that $R=A/I$ is a regular local ring and $\dim A=\dim R+r$, with $r=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}P^{\rm gp}$. The local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Noetherian because $X$ is locally Noetherian, so its strict henselization $A$ is Noetherian [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian].

source.place: Expose VI 1.2 and 1.6, printed pp. 69--70: the log-regular local criterion and the chart modelled on P at the geometric point.

proof.text: Put $n=\dim R$ and choose a regular system of parameters $\bar t_1,\ldots,\bar t_n$ of $R$, with lifts $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in A$. Since $\mathfrak m_R=(\bar t_1,\ldots,\bar t_n)$, the maximal ideal of $A$ is $\mathfrak m_A=I+(t_1,\ldots,t_n)=(a(q)\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)A$. The completion $\widehat A$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ and residue field $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], complete for $\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal](1), and $\dim\widehat A=\dim A=n+r$ [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension]. Apply the Cohen presentation [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-power-series-presentation] to $\widehat A$ and restrict its surjection to the coefficient ring: this gives a ring map $\lambda:\Lambda\to\widehat A$ with $\Lambda$ a field mapping isomorphically to $k$ when $\operatorname{char}k=0$, and a Cohen ring $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda/p\Lambda\cong k$ when $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. If $A$ contains a field, then either $\operatorname{char}k=0$ and we put $L=\Lambda$, or $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, the field has characteristic $p$, $p=0$ in $\widehat A$, and $\lambda$ factors through $\Lambda/p\Lambda\cong k$; in both cases $L=k$ is a coefficient field of $\widehat A$. If $A$ contains no field, then $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ (otherwise every nonzero integer is a unit of the local ring $A$ and $\mathbf Q\subset A$), and we put $L=C=\Lambda$. Define $\phi_0:L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to\widehat A$ by $cz^qt^e\mapsto\lambda(c)a(q)t^e$; it is a ring map because $a$ is a monoid map to $(A,\cdot)$, and it sends the finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak a=(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ into $\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ (in the Cohen case $\lambda(p)=p\in\mathfrak m_A$ since $\operatorname{char}k=p$). As $\widehat A$ is complete, $\phi_0$ induces compatible maps $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]/\mathfrak a^j\to\widehat A/\mathfrak m_A^j\widehat A$ and hence a continuous local map $\phi:B_L(P,n)\to\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] with $\phi(z^q)=a(q)$ and $\phi(t_i)=t_i$. Surjectivity: $B_L(P,n)$ is complete for $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak aB_L(P,n)$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal](1); $\mathfrak n\widehat A$ is generated by $p$ (Cohen case), the $a(q)$ and the $t_i$, so it equals $\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$, for which $\widehat A$ is Hausdorff; and $B_L(P,n)\to\widehat A/\mathfrak m_A\widehat A=k$ is onto because $\Lambda\to k$ is. Hence $\phi$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal].

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (the presentation of the completed strict local ring by the chart monomials and parameters), with Kato (1994), Theorem 3.2 WANTED locally; the Cohen-presentation and complete-surjectivity argument is written out by the agent.

proof.text: Put $D=L[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. It is a complete regular Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_D=(\mathfrak m_L,t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ and $\dim D=n$ if $L=k$, $\dim D=n+1$ if $L=C$; in the Cohen case $p,t_1,\ldots,t_n$ is a regular system of parameters, since these $n+1=\dim D$ elements generate $\mathfrak m_D$ [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete]. For every $j$ the inclusion $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]\subset D[P]$ induces an isomorphism $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]/\mathfrak a^j\cong D[P]/\mathfrak a_D^j$, $\mathfrak a_D=(\mathfrak m_D,z^q\ (q\neq0))$, because $\mathfrak a^j$ contains every monomial $t^e$ with $|e|\ge j$ and $D/\mathfrak m_D^j=L[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\mathfrak m_L,t_1,\ldots,t_n)^j$; passing to the limit, $B_L(P,n)$ is the ring $H$ of [lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension] for $(D,T=P)$, with $N_H=(z^q:q\neq0)H$ and $H/N_H\cong D$. That lemma gives: $B_L(P,n)$ is a Noetherian local integral domain of dimension $\dim D+r$, i.e. $n+r$ for $L=k$ and $n+r+1$ for $L=C$; and for $\eta$ with $\overline\eta\in\mathfrak m_D\setminus\mathfrak m_D^2$, $\eta$ is a nonzerodivisor and $\dim B_L(P,n)/(\eta)=\dim D+r-1$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: the model rings k[[P]][[t_1,...,t_n]] and C(k)[[P]][[t_1,...,t_n]]/(f); their dimension and domain properties are taken from the cited model lemma.

proof.text: Equal characteristic ($A$ contains a field, $L=k$). By Steps 2 and 3, $\phi:B_k(P,n)\to\widehat A$ is a surjection from a Noetherian local domain of dimension $n+r$ onto a ring of dimension $n+r$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. If $K=\ker\phi\neq0$, every prime of $B_k(P,n)$ containing $K$ is nonzero, so every chain of primes of $\widehat A\cong B_k(P,n)/K$ gives a chain of primes of $B_k(P,n)$ that can be lengthened by $(0)$, and $\dim B_k(P,n)\ge\dim\widehat A+1$, a contradiction. Hence $\phi$ is an isomorphism $B_k(P,n)\cong\widehat A$ with $z^q\mapsto a(q)$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i), printed p. 70; Kato (1994), Theorem 3.2 WANTED locally. The equal-dimension injectivity argument is written by the agent.

proof.text: Mixed characteristic ($A$ contains no field, $L=C$, $\operatorname{char}k=p$). Let $J=(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. Since $\phi$ is surjective, $\phi(J)$ is the ideal of $\widehat A$ generated by the $a(q)$ and the $t_i$, which is $\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ by Step 2; as $p\in\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$, choose $j\in J$ with $\phi(j)=p$ and put $\theta=p-j$. Then $\theta\in\ker\phi$ and $\theta-p\in J$. Modulo $N_H=(z^q:q\neq0)$, $\overline\theta\in D=C[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ is congruent to $p$ modulo $(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$; as $p,t_1,\ldots,t_n$ is a regular system of parameters of $D$ (Step 3), $\overline\theta\in\mathfrak m_D\setminus\mathfrak m_D^2$. By [lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension], $\dim B_C(P,n)/(\theta)=(n+1)+r-1=n+r$, and by [lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality](ii), applicable since $\theta-p\in J$, $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$ is a (normal) integral domain; it is Noetherian local as a quotient of $B_C(P,n)$. Thus $\phi$ induces a surjection $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)\to\widehat A$ from a Noetherian local domain of dimension $n+r$ onto a ring of dimension $n+r$ (Step 2), and the argument of Step 4 shows that it is injective. Hence $\ker\phi=(\theta)$ and $\widehat A\cong B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$, compatibly with $z^q\mapsto a(q)$, where $C$ is a Cohen ring with residue field $k$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $\theta-p\in J$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(ii), printed p. 70 ('f est congru a p modulo l'ideal engendre par P-{0} et les t_i'); Kato (1994), Theorem 3.2 WANTED locally. The principal-kernel argument by dimension and the domain property of the model is written by the agent.

proof.text: Compatibility with the chart is built into the construction: $\phi(z^q)=a(q)$ for every $q\in P$, where $a$ is the structural map of the chart $P\to M|_W$ on the affine pointed etale neighbourhood $W'=W$ of Step 1 [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart, def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], which induces the chosen identification of $P$ with $\overline M_{\bar x}$. So the isomorphisms of Steps 4 and 5 are the asserted ones, with the (trivial) chart replacement allowed by the statement.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6, printed p. 70: 'X admet une carte modelee sur P en x, qui donne lieu a des isomorphismes'.

proof.text: Boundary cases. For $P=\{0\}$ there are no monomials $z^q$ with $q\ne0$, $I=0$ and $A=R$ is regular; for $n=0$ there are no $t_i$ and $\mathfrak m_A=I$. The construction of Steps 2--5 goes through unchanged, with $\mathfrak m_k=0$ and $\mathfrak m_C=pC$ in the completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Both happen together only when $A$ is a field, hence in the equal-characteristic case, where $\widehat A=A=k=B_k(\{0\},0)$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, notation and boundary cases.

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned split by replacing the one-line appeal to Kato with an explicit construction. The proof keeps the sharp chart, lifts a regular system of parameters of A/I, builds the continuous surjection B_L(P,n)->completion of A from the Cohen presentation and the complete-source surjectivity criterion, and identifies the kernel by dimension: the model ring is a Noetherian local domain of the same dimension in equal characteristic, and in mixed characteristic an element theta=p-j of the kernel with theta-p in the monomial/parameter ideal gives a domain quotient of the same dimension. Model properties come from the existing lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension and lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality. The item statement and edge cases are unchanged. Maintainer review (2026-10-18): dropped the delivered node lem-trf-log-regular-completed-model-dimension, a conjunction of special cases of those two existing nodes, and rewrote Steps 2--5 (the initial-form and p-adic cancellation sketches were not arguments; the completion facts were uncited).

Steps 2, 4 and 5 compare dimensions through dim of completion = dim A, a generic fact.
Step 3 needs L[[t_1..t_n]] to be complete regular local of the stated dimension to apply the model-ring lemma.
